title: logsift analyze and monitor --format json
description: One analysis of one log: the errors and warnings found in it, the pre-commit hooks it names, and their counts. `logsift analyze --format json` prints it for a log file, and `logsift monitor --format json` prints it for a command's output with a summary of the run added. Each saved analysis under $XDG_CACHE_HOME/logsift/json/ holds the same document. A change that renames or removes a field, or changes a field's meaning, raises schema_version.

schema_version.description: The version of this shape. A reader checks it before trusting any other field.

summary.description: The monitored run. Present only from `logsift monitor`, because `logsift analyze` reads a file and ran nothing.

status.description: success when the command exited 0, else failed.

exit_code.description: The command's exit status, which logsift monitor also exits with.

duration_seconds.description: Wall time from starting the command to its exit.

command.description: The command and its arguments, joined by single spaces.

log_file.description: The raw log saved under $XDG_CACHE_HOME/logsift/raw/. Null when the run saved no log.

errors.description: Each line found to be an error, in log order.

warnings.description: Each line found to be a warning, in log order.

hooks.description: Pre-commit hooks named on a `name.....Passed` or `name.....Failed` line, each listed once.

issue.description: One error or warning. A line is one when a JSON or key=value log line says level error or warning, or when a TOML pattern matches its message. The pattern fields are absent for the first kind.

id.description: Its position among the errors, or among the warnings, counting from 1.

message.description: The line as logged, with ANSI escapes and a leading ISO timestamp removed.

line_in_log.description: The line's number in the log, counting from 1.

format.description: How the parser read the line.

pattern_name.description: The name of the TOML pattern that matched.

suggestion.description: The matching pattern's fix hint, where it has one.

pattern_context_lines_after.description: How many lines after this one the matching pattern asked to keep, which context_after then holds in place of the default two.

code.description: A linter or tool code found in the message, such as F401, SC2086, FURB101, arg-type or B101.

timestamp.description: The line's timestamp, where the parser found one.

file.description: Copied from a JSON or key=value log line that carries a file field.

file_line.description: Copied from a JSON or key=value log line that carries a file_line field.

file_references.description: Each file:line reference found in the message, in the order found. Each is a two-item array: the path as a string, then the line as an integer.

context_before.description: Up to two parsed lines before this one. Blank lines are skipped.

context_after.description: Parsed lines after this one: two, or pattern_context_lines_after where set.

log_entry.description: One parsed log line. A JSON line keeps every field it had, and a key=value line every pair, beside the fields named here.

line_number.description: The line's number in the log, counting from 1.

level.description: The line's own level field, or INFO where it has none. Patterns decide a plain line's severity, not this.

message.description: The line's message, empty for a key=value line with no message pair.

timestamp.description: A leading ISO timestamp, or a JSON line's own timestamp field.
